<h2>Save Functional-Type Classification for One Continental Unit</h2>

<h3>Description</h3>

<p>Saves a pre-computed functional-type classification tibble as a
dated '.qs' file in 'path_processed'. The classification is
produced upstream by 'assign_functional_type_clusters()' via the
'ft_result_continent' pipeline target.
</p>


<h3>Usage</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>save_continental_functional_type_classification(
  continent_id,
  data_functional_type_classification,
  path_classification_directory = here::here("Data/Processed/Traits"),
  classification_source_prefix = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE
)
</code></pre>


<h3>Arguments</h3>

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td><code id="continent_id">continent_id</code></td>
<td>
<p>A single non-empty character string identifying the continental
unit (e.g. '&quot;europe&quot;', '&quot;america&quot;', '&quot;asia&quot;'). Used only for
naming the output file.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="data_functional_type_classification">data_functional_type_classification</code></td>
<td>
<p>A data frame containing the functional-type classification, as
returned in the 'classification' element of
'assign_functional_type_clusters()'. Typically has columns
'taxon_name', 'functional_type', and 'silhouette_width'.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="path_classification_directory">path_classification_directory</code></td>
<td>
<p>A single character string giving the directory where the '.qs'
output file will be written. Default:
'here::here(&quot;Data/Processed/Traits&quot;)'.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="classification_source_prefix">classification_source_prefix</code></td>
<td>
<p>Optional single non-empty character string to prepend to the
'continent_id' portion of the file name. Use 'NULL' (default)
for the historical paleo/global naming convention, or '&quot;modern&quot;'
for modern-data functional-type classifications.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="verbose">verbose</code></td>
<td>
<p>Logical. If 'TRUE' (default), progress messages are printed
to the console via 'cli'.</p>
</td></tr>
</table>


<h3>Details</h3>

<p>**Steps performed**:
</p>

<ol>
<li><p> Validate arguments.
</p>
</li>
<li><p> Save 'data_functional_type_classification' with
'RUtilpol::save_latest_file()' as a dated '.qs' file in
'path_classification_directory'. The file is only overwritten when the
content has changed since the previous version.
</p>
</li>
<li><p> Resolve the path of the just-saved file via
'RUtilpol::get_latest_file_name()'.
</p>
</li>
<li><p> Return the file path as a character string.
</p>
</li></ol>

<p>Data filtering, distance computation, hierarchical clustering,
ft-groups selection are all handled upstream by
'select_continental_trait_table()', 'compute_trait_dissimilarity()',
'fit_hierarchical_clustering()', and 'assign_functional_type_clusters()' respectively.
</p>


<h3>Value</h3>

<p>A single character string: the absolute path to the '.qs' file
that was written. The file is saved via
'RUtilpol::save_latest_file()' using the name stem
'data_ft_classification_continent_id'
when 'classification_source_prefix = NULL', or
'data_ft_classification_classification_source_prefix_continent_id'
otherwise. The final file name includes a date stamp and
content hash appended by 'RUtilpol' (e.g.
'data_ft_classification_europe_2026-05-07__abc123__.qs').
</p>


<h3>See Also</h3>

<p>[select_continental_trait_table()],
[compute_trait_dissimilarity()], [fit_hierarchical_clustering()],
[assign_functional_type_clusters()]
</p>
